div.head: Ps Cn for 17
div.ab: Si quis autem co[ram] primarium pugnauerit in placito, emendet secundum pretium sui ipsius, quod Angli ƿere et ƿite dicunt, et soluat primario quadraginta solidos.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 623 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if anyone fights in a plea [befo]re a chief man, let him pay compensation according to his own price, which the English call ƿere and ƿite (wergild and wite), and let him pay the chief man forty shillings.

note.seg: Verf. missversteht die Vorlage, die nur wer mit pretium übersetzt, und stellt den Primar offenbar ganz willkürlich statt des comes ein
The author misunderstands his source, which merely translates wer by pretium, and puts in the primarius, evidently quite arbitrarily, instead of the comes
